observations: body L1-L3, L9: the dash before «Nihili» measures 10.1 pt. The year 306 of the Hijra began on 14 June 918; «Ibn Surayǵ» is letter-spaced, its ǵ with the acute, as «Ǵābir» (L9).
body L4: the year 288 of the Hijra began on 26 December 900, and Thābit ibn Qurrah died in February 901.
body L6, L9: «Al–Bīrūnī», «176–77» and «al–Battānī» have long dashes (5.3, 5.4 and 5.4 pt). The bold italic c is note c), which begins in L20; the method of Thābit is announced for its end.

body L11, L20: the dashes after «b)» and «c)» measure 10.3 and 9.4 pt, the hyphen of «2-8» 3.7 pt; «17—pag.» has a dash of 8.5 pt. The places are p. 86, L3-L8 (those who erred in the visibility of the new moon) and p. 86, L17 to p. 87, the last line (al-Battānī's rule for the visibility).
body L16-L18: «al–mīqāt» has a long dash (5.3 pt); the second l of «aequinoctialium» prints damaged.
body L22: a heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which goes on to p. 267.

notes_left L1-L12: note 2 of p. 265 concluded. The dash before «Muslimi» measures 8.6 pt; the hyphen at the end of L1 prints short (1.2 pt), and «gra» (L6) is printed without its hyphen, a speck standing in its place. «t I,» (L10) is printed without a stop; «al-» (L9) has a hyphen (3.5 pt). The Arabic of L5 is «over the whole world», that of L12 «two stages», the «bidui iter».
notes_left L13-L15: note 1 begins; it goes on in the right column. «al-Ǵabartī» is letter-spaced, with Ǵ.

notes_right L1-L12: the end of note 1. A short bar prints over the end of «quo» (L3). The dash before «Ibn al-Fāriḍ» (L6) is printed broken in two pieces (1.9 and 4.4 pt). The last day of ramaḍān 1217 fell on 24 January 1803, the first of shawwāl 1235 on 12 July 1820. The verse (L9) is printed as two hemistichs side by side, the first on the right, «انه» without hamza; the dots of the final yāʾ of «عيني» reach down into L10. Ibn al-Fāriḍ died on 2 Jumādā I 632, 23 January 1235.

notes_right L1-L12: Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXV) add to note 1 an example from Aḥmad ibn Khālid an-Nāṣirī as-Salāwī, Kitāb al-istiqṣā’ (Cairo 1312 H., vol. IV, p. 245): in the night between the 28th and the 29th of ramaḍān 1292 (28-29 October 1875) twelve men at Rabāṭ declared they had seen the new moon after sunset; the qāḍī accepted their testimony, wrote to the sultan, and on the 29th the fast was ended; the court astronomers held that the day could not be the feast; after sunset on the 29th the new moon was sought in vain in a clear sky, the fast was resumed until the 30th, when the new moon was seen at last, and the witnesses were imprisoned for their fraud. The conjunction fell on 29 October 1875, at about 5 hours Greenwich time, so that no crescent could be seen on the evening of the 28th.
notes_right L13-L15: note 2 corrects Suter's title of Thābit's epistle (L4-L5 of the text); «150,v.–151,v.» (note 3) has a long dash (4.3 pt).

notes_right L1-L12: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XVII; AB01-PDF0434-body-L022 to L025), on Part I, p. LXXV and this page, give other examples of the Muslims' uncertainty in sighting the new moon and fixing the beginning of the month: Ibn Ǵubayr, The travels of Ibn Jubair, ed. W. Wright (Leyden 1852), pp. 163, 168-170 and 172 (in Schiaparelli's Italian translation, Rome 1906, pp. 144, 150-152 and 154); and jesting verses on the day of doubt (يوم الشك) by Abū Nuwās, al-Fukāhah wa ’l-īlinās fī muǵūn Abī Nuwās (Cairo 1316 H.), p. 114.
